claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^−4–10^−2 s^−1.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
A dense, adherent Al2O3 coating approximately 1 μm thick can be deposited on HfNbTaTiZr by PVD.
The deposited Al2O3 coating will remain continuous and well adhered during exposure at 1000 °C in air for about 100 hours.
A continuous Al2O3 surface layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr.
Al2O3 is sufficiently chemically inert and thermally stable to serve as a protective scale at 1000 °C in air.
The Al2O3 coating will significantly slow oxygen ingress into the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
Slower oxygen ingress will reduce internal oxidation of HfNbTaTiZr.
Applying the surface coating will not alter the cast alloy microstructure that governs its mechanical performance.
The coated alloy will exhibit less oxide-scale growth than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after exposure at 1000 °C in air for about 100 hours.
The coated alloy will exhibit less internal oxygen penetration than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after exposure at 1000 °C in air for about 100 hours.
The coating will preserve the alloy's baseline high-temperature yield strength under loading at strain rates of 10^−4–10^−2 s^−1.
The coating will preserve the alloy's baseline tensile ductility.
